name: Nicolas Sarkozy
summary: Nicolas Sarkozy, French president from 2007 to 2012 from the centre-right UMP, campaigned for a stronger, more market-oriented France while calling after 2008 for a regulated capitalism, a financial transactions tax, the end of tax havens and a bigger role for Europe. He rejoined NATO's integrated command, led the 2011 Libya intervention and backed a Palestinian state alongside Israel's security.

notes: First audit of a living person. Read by theme: his 2007 address to Congress, his UN General Assembly speeches of 2008, 2009 and 2011, his three Toulon economic addresses (2008, 2009, 2011, Élysée texts), and 2007-2012 television transcripts in MediaSum (financial transactions tax, Libya, Iran, immigration). The French laws of his presidency (LEGI) were searched but a law is cited only where he drove it in his own words, which the sources opened do not show, so the answers cite a law only for the four laws where a speech of his shows his drive. Versailles 2009 is read from the Élysée text and Famille chrétienne 2012 from vie-publique.fr (rendered with headless Chrome). The 2010 pension law (age 62), the 2007 service minimum law, the 2008 constitutional reform and the 2011 Besson law were searched in LEGI but settle no statement here or lack a drive source; the pension law and Besson law are therefore not cited. Not read: the 2007 UN speech beyond the first pages, his books (no open text found), and his Senate-era and Interior Ministry record.
